review.rationale: The complete unmodified production Android fingerprint exactly equals the runtime embedded in the published v1.0.2 APK. expo-application 58.1.2 was already in the resolved native graph through expo-notifications; declaring that same dependency directly does not alter it. The classifier now permits dependency declaration/lockfile changes only when this full raw fingerprint matches, without restoring, skipping or normalizing dependency inputs. Native source, build-hook, fingerprint configuration/ignore and unknown build-script guards remain in force; failure or mismatch does not authorize OTA. Deterministic review-context now selects update with no exemptions or unresolved blockers. Existing source binding, APK identity/version checks and guarded runtime-preserving production publication remain required.
evidence: publishedBaseline verified stable APK v1.0.2, source 710bd2e10b4eb8aa16378486f3cb3517770ac878, successful master build run 40502268634 and archived EAS build d51d8be5-d5a1-4f8e-897e-71fd22381369: version 1.0.2, versionCode 3, production channel, runtime 4a7adc844a392bfaead47665719d0291b9f3da58. APK source belongs to origin/master.

Compared the complete APK-to-source file list and master-to-source diff. app.json, app.config.js, eas.json, config/, modules/, native plugins, launcher/splash assets, native hooks and ignore files remain unchanged from the APK. New PNGs and steam effects are loaded/rendered by JavaScript with existing React Native/SVG modules.

The root dependency/lockfile declaration of expo-application ~58.1.2 is the sole dependency edit. Its existing resolved lock entry is unchanged at 58.1.2, already required by expo-notifications. No new package version or native module enters the resolved graph.

With no fileHookTransform, the production SDK fingerprint is 4a7adc844a392bfaead47665719d0291b9f3da58, exactly matching the published APK. review-context now reports mode=update, compatible=true, match=exact, exemptions=[], reasons=[]. rawRuntime and normalizedRuntime both equal the APK runtime; no normalization was applied.

compareNativeFingerprints first verifies metadata and old/new hook guards. Only dependency declaration fields and package-lock are eligible for exact raw proof. It never normalizes dependency contents. Raw failure/invalid hash rejects the check; mismatch retains the conservative APK path for changed dependencies/lockfiles. Unknown native/build/config/ignore changes remain blocked.

The existing administrative normalization path remains restricted to previously audited deployment scripts and temporary ignore additions when dependency inputs are unchanged. Tests verify the raw path has no transform and dependency mismatches cannot fall through to normalization.

New regression tests cover same-graph dependency promotion, lockfile mismatch, different native hash, failed/invalid hash calculation, missing APK baseline, native source/config/unknown script/hook/ignore guards and preservation of the legacy administrative normalization path. Full local lint/typecheck and 237 tests pass.

Inspected check.yml, cloud-build.yml, publish-release.yml, publish-web.yml, eas.json, app.config.js, deployment.mjs, deployment-review.mjs, deployment-history.mjs, check-release.mjs and release-candidate.mjs. Production plan and the guarded publisher invoke the same nativeCompatibility implementation and revalidate the report/source/APK. The publisher verifies runtime and commit, promotes same-source web only after successful OTA, then records a revision Release while retaining APK Latest.

Release notes compare with successful production update v1.0.2-r1 at ffb6ba236cd8a3ecf283750cfe4ba9babf2072e4; native compatibility compares with v1.0.2. Candidate includes skins/effects, black-cat home placement, release summaries and user version reporting. App version 1.0.2 and Android versionCode 3 remain unchanged for OTA.

Version reporting migration 20261029025831 is already applied and its transactional role/admission/timestamp/upsert tests rolled back all observations. This rule/review update does not alter the database, publish production code, grant skins or dispatch notifications.
